newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asia's per capita oil, gas reserves world's lowest.
newsitem.headline: Asia's per capita oil, gas reserves world's lowest.

text.p: Asia's per capita crude and natural gas reserves are by far the smallest in the world, and are expected to dwindle due to rapid economic and population growth, an energy researcher said on Monday.

"Crude reserves per person are estimated at 13 barrels in Asia, as opposed to 4,400 barrels in the Middle East and 300 barrels in North America," Yohji Uchiyama, senior researcher at the Central Research Institute of Electric Power Industry, told a seminar.
"With the region's population exploding, it is without doubt that the disparity will grow," he said.

Asia also comes at the bottom in terms of natural gas reserves, with 2,900 cubic metres of recoverable gas per person, compared with 301,000 cubic metres in the Middle East and 136,000 cubic metres in the former Soviet Union and eastern Europe, he said.
Asia's per capita gas reserves are one-fourth of those in Central and South America, the region with the second-lowest per capita reserves.

Asian countries currently satisfy more than 50 percent of their crude requirements with imports from the Middle East, compared with western Europe's 29 percent and 10 percent for North America, he said.
